summary.title: Story-telling with Git rebase
summary.one_liner: Learn how to use interactive Git rebase to revise commit history before sharing it, writing clearer commits and handling conflicts and auto-squashing.
keywords: clean up git history before pushing
takeaways: Rebasing lets you revise development history before sharing it with the team.
Good Git commit messages record the intent of code changes, making future changes easier.
Interactive rebasing mechanics: reordering, editing and combining commits.
How to merge conflicts during a rebase without losing code.
How to auto-squash commits and make feature branches less painful.
summary.summary: This talk-style page, dated November 30, 2018, argues that version control communicates intent over a project's lifetime and that rebasing lets you revise history before sharing it. It covers writing commit messages that track intent, using feature branches effectively, the mechanics of interactive rebase, resolving conflicts without losing code, and auto-squashing commits. The description is brief and the aim is to make developers comfortable with interactive rebasing.
